selection: The 2 October audit (eval-feasibility/redline-task-audit.md): criteria classed U (transfer as written) and A (transfer with output adaptation) are judged; I (incompatible) are excluded with the audit's reason. Adapted wording in layer-c/criteria.mjs.

criteria.adapted: Section 1.7, the definition of "Derivative Work" ("“Derivative Work” means a work which is based upon one or more preexisting works ..."), which LargeCo restored, stays in the agreement: no proposed change deletes the definition or removes the defined term.

attorney.criterion: Accepts Section 1.7 LargeCo's restoration of "Derivative Works"
attorney.justification: LargCo is correct in rejecting deletion of Derivative works as it is used throughout the document. Deleting this definition would result in confusion as to what that term means.

criteria.adapted: In the definition of "User Information" (Section 1.19), the output proposes deleting the reference to "User data" (limb (b): "all User data that is generated, collected, stored, processed or used in connection with or derived from Provider’s performance of the Services"), so the definition no longer conflicts with the statement at its end about what User Information does not include. Wording with the same effect counts; an explanation without a proposed change does not.

attorney.criterion: Deletes of Section 1.19 LargeCo's reference to "User Data" in the definition of "User Information".
attorney.justification: By not deleting the statement, it conflicts with AgentCo's addition that User Information does not include User Data.

criteria.adapted: In Section 2.2 (LargeCo's paragraph beginning "LargeCo may permit its Affiliates and their Authorized Users to access and use the Services"), the output proposes deleting the word "Authorized", so the provision refers to "Users" (the defined term) rather than "Authorized Users" (Provider personnel given access to LargeCo systems). Deleting it at each place in that paragraph, or wording with the same effect, counts.

attorney.criterion: Deletes in Section 2.2 the word "Authorized" .
attorney.justification: The capitalized term of "Authorized User" is incorrect. The correct term is "User". By referencing "Authorized User", it is referencing the wrong type of User thereby allowing non-LargeCo employees to use their licenses.

criteria.adapted: In Section 2.3.2, LargeCo's inserted sentence "The foregoing does not authorize Provider to disclose LargeCo’s actual AI Inputs or AI Outputs (in whole or part) to any third party, and any AI Input or AI Output that contains LargeCo Data, User Information, Personal Information, or other LargeCo Confidential Information remains LargeCo’s Confidential Information regardless of similarity to inputs or outputs of other customers" stays in substance: no proposed change deletes or weakens it.

attorney.criterion: Accepts in Section 2.3.2 LargeCo's insertion of "The foregoing does not authorize Provider to disclose LargeCo’s actual AI Inputs or AI Outputs (in whole or part) to any third party, and any AI Input or AI Output that contains LargeCo Data, User Information, Personal Information, or other LargeCo Confidential Information remains LargeCo’s Confidential Information regardless of similarity to inputs or outputs of other customers".
attorney.justification: In Section 2.3.2- Since the AI inputs and AI outputs will contain LargeCo's Confidential information, AgentCo is ok accepting that clarification.

criteria.adapted: In Section 2.3.2, the output proposes restoring the sentence LargeCo deleted, "Queries submitted by, and responses delivered to other customers and their users do not constitute LargeCo’s Confidential Information", or wording with the same effect (outputs delivered to other customers are not LargeCo's Confidential Information merely because they resemble LargeCo's).

attorney.criterion: Rejects in Section 2.3.2 LargeCo's deletion of  "Queries submitted by, and responses delivered to other customers and their users do not constitute LargeCo’s Confidential Information"
attorney.justification: Section 2.3.2-AgentCo must be clear that even though AI Outputs may be substantially similar to LargeCo's, it will not be considered LargeCo's Confidential information because it did not use LargeCo's Confidential Information.

criteria.adapted: In Section 2.3.4 (Third-Party AI Technology), item (c) reads "... a written agreement with the licensor of such AI Technology that imposes obligations that impose obligations substantially consistent ...". The output proposes deleting the duplicated words "that impose obligations" that LargeCo inserted, leaving the clause otherwise as it stands.

attorney.criterion: Deletes in Section 2.3.4 LargeCo's insertion of "that impose obligations".
attorney.justification: LargeCo inserted language that was already in the clause. Just deleted duplicate language.

criteria.adapted: In Section 2.3.4 (Third-Party AI Technology), item (c), LargeCo's replacement of "at least as restrictive as those imposed on or required of Provider" with "substantially consistent with the relevant obligations of Provider" stays: no proposed change restores "at least as restrictive" or otherwise makes the standard stricter.

attorney.criterion: Accepts in Section 2.3.4 LargeCo's replacement of the term "at least as restrictive" with "substantially consistent"
attorney.justification: The term "substantially consistent" is a less restrictive obligation then "at least as restrictive" that is favorable to AgentCo, but it will hurt LargeCo because it allows AgentCo's Vendor to not necessarily have the same restrictive obligations as AgentCo.

criteria.adapted: In Section 3.1 (Restrictions), item (f) prohibits probing, scanning or attempting to penetrate the Service, and LargeCo added "except for security testing of LargeCo’s own configuration, integrations, and Authorized User behavior or as otherwise expressly permitted by Provider in writing". The output proposes removing that exception, or rewriting it so that LargeCo gains no right to test, probe or scan Provider's systems beyond what Provider permits in writing.

attorney.criterion: Rejects in Section 3.1 LargeCo's addition of "except for security testing of LargeCo’s own configuration, integrations, and Authorized User behavior or as otherwise expressly permitted by Provider in writing"
attorney.justification: Section 3.1-This addition allows LargeCo to penetrate, probe, and scan AgentCo's systems. Regardless of the reason, it would be a non-starter for most software that is performing this function. This  type of testing should be reserved for critical services. Allowing penetration, probing, or scanning is indistinguishable from a malicious attack. These activities can't be allowed safely without losing control of our threat model.

criteria.adapted: LargeCo's inserted Section 8, "Term and Termination" (heading "TERM AND TERMINATION." and its subsections), stays in the agreement as a section: no proposed change deletes the section as a whole. Changes to individual termination rights, renumbering or cross-reference corrections do not count against this criterion.

attorney.criterion: Accepts in Section 8 LargeCo's insertion of  Section 8 "Term and Termination" Clause.
attorney.justification: This clause is important because it allows the parties to not only set the term of the contract but allows parties to terminate the contract. Without this language, a court could rule this an evergreen contract that can't be terminated.

criteria.adapted: In Section 14.1 (General Cap), LargeCo inserted a floor so the cap is "the greater of (a) the total of all payments actually received by Provider ... during the twelve (12) month period ... or (b) US$1,000,000". The output proposes deleting the US$1,000,000 alternative so the general cap is the fees paid in the preceding twelve months.

attorney.criterion: Rejects in Section 14.1 LargeCo's insertion of "or $1,000,000"
attorney.justification: This follows AgentCo's policy that the Liability should only be capped to the fees paid in the preceding 12 months from claim.

criteria.adapted: The output proposes removing LargeCo's inserted "Exceptions to Indirect-Damages Exclusion. The exclusion set forth in Section 11.4 shall not apply to, and shall not limit liability arising from: (i) Provider's breach of Confidentiality; (ii) Provider's breach of Training; (iii) Provider's breach of Data Security or Exhibit C; (iv) any Party's indemnification obligations; or (v) fraud, gross negligence, or willful misconduct", or a change with the same effect (the indirect-damages exclusion applies without those exceptions).

attorney.criterion:
Rejects in Section 16.7 LargeCo's insertion of  "16.7.	Exceptions to Indirect-Damages Exclusion. The exclusion set forth in Section 11.4 shall not apply to, and shall not limit liability arising from:
16.8.	(i) Provider's breach of Confidentiality; (ii) Provider's breach of Training; (iii) Provider's breach of Data Security or Exhibit C; (iv) any Party's indemnification obligations; or (v) fraud, gross negligence, or willful misconduct."
attorney.justification: Indirect damages are inherently speculative, potentially unlimited which would bankrupt a company, and not aligned with the economic framework of this Agreement or available insurance coverage. Removing these breaches from the Indirect damages cap would introduce a disproportionate and unquantifiable risks, which is not commercially reasonable.

criteria.adapted: In Section 15.1 (Indemnification Obligations), LargeCo inserted item (a) "Provider's breach of Confidentiality, Training, Data Security, Exhibit C, or any Applicable Law applicable to Provider's performance under this Agreement" and item (c) "the fraud, gross negligence, or willful misconduct of Provider". The output proposes deleting both, so Provider's indemnity covers only third-party infringement claims (item (b)). Deleting only one of the two fails.

attorney.criterion: Rejects in Section 15.1. LargeCo's insertion of Section 15.1(a) and 15.1(c).
attorney.justification: Section 15.1 (a) and (c) Our firm position was that we only offer infringement indemnification.

criteria.adapted: In the warranty disclaimer (Section 12(k), last paragraph), LargeCo's opening "Except for the warranties expressly set forth in this Agreement (including Sections 2.3 (AI), ... (Reps & Warranties), ... (Indemnification), and Exhibit C)" stays in substance: no proposed change deletes it or narrows the warranties it preserves. Correcting its section cross-references does not count against this criterion.

attorney.criterion: Accepts in Section 12(k) LargeCo's  addition of "Except for warranties expressly set forth in this Agreement (including Sections 2.3 (AI), 12 (Reps & Warranties), 15 (Indemnification), and Exhibit C)"
attorney.justification: 12.k Beginning of last paragraph. This redline correctly recognizes that warranties appear in other clauses. By failing to carve them out, those warranties would have been invalidated.
